questions.question: Cidofovir.

parts.text: What is it active against other than Herpesviridae? Name three.

parts_raw.text: What is it active against other than herpesviridae?  Name three.

questions.model_answer: Cidofovir is a nucleotide (cytosine) analogue that inhibits viral DNA polymerase, so it has broad activity against DNA viruses: (1) Adenoviridae (adenovirus); (2) Polyomaviridae (BK and JC virus); (3) Poxviridae (vaccinia, variola, monkeypox, molluscum contagiosum). (Papillomaviridae/HPV, e.g. recurrent respiratory papillomatosis, is a further acceptable family.)
questions.beyond_mandell: Cidofovir is not covered in this chapter (Miscellaneous Antiviral Agents); answer from Mandell antiviral chapter and established knowledge.

cohort_answer.text: MOA: inhibits viral DNA polymerase, therefore active for other DNA viruses. Adenovirus; Polyomavirus (BK and JC); Papillomavirus (HPV); Poxvirus (vaccinia, variola...theoretically)

questions.question: Cidofovir.

parts.text: Name three non-herpes viruses it is indicated for.

parts_raw.text: a) Name 3 non-herpes viruses it is indicated for?

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Adenovirus (severe infection in the immunocompromised); (2) Polyomavirus (BK/JC virus); (3) Papillomavirus (HPV, e.g. intralesional therapy for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis). Poxviruses (smallpox/variola, vaccinia) are an additional acceptable answer. Its sole FDA-approved indication is CMV retinitis in AIDS; the others are off-label. As an acyclic nucleotide phosphonate it bypasses the viral kinase activation step and relies on cellular kinases, accounting for its broad DNA-virus activity and nephrotoxicity.
questions.beyond_mandell: Cidofovir is not covered in this chapter; answer from established knowledge and IDSA/Mandell antiviral pharmacology.

cohort_answer.text: Only works on DNA viruses. FDA: CMV retinitis in AIDS patients. Non-FDA: Adenovirus infx in severe immunosuppression; local injection in recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (HPV); JC Virus/BK virus (polyomavirus); Smallpox (no clinical data). Monophosphate nucleotide analogue, NOT phosphorylated by viral kinase unlike acyclovir/ganciclovir, requires cell kinases - more toxicity

questions.question: Ebola.

parts.text: Name three places the virus can persist after symptoms resolve.

parts_raw.text: 3 places the virus can persist after symptoms resolve

questions.model_answer:
a) (1) Cerebrospinal fluid / CNS — meningoencephalitis can occur months after initial diagnosis, with infectious virus recovered from CSF. (2) Aqueous humor of the eye — uveitis presenting 1-2 years after infection. (3) Seminal fluid — virus persists for over a year, enabling sexual transmission.
b) Remdesivir (GS-5734) is a nucleotide (adenosine) analog prodrug; after intracellular conversion to its active triphosphate it is incorporated by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and causes delayed chain termination, blocking viral RNA replication.
questions.beyond_mandell: Persistence sites and remdesivir mechanism are not detailed in this Mandell slice; from UpToDate/product data.

cohort_answer.text: Patients can develop late manifestations after recovering from the initial illness. CSF - meningitis has occurred months after initial diagnosis (infectious virus recovered in CSF). Aqueous fluid - uveitis can occur 1-2 years after initial infection. Seminal fluid - persisted for over 1 year.
